headline: A freelance journalist says a company called Handshake offered $1,000 for a set of reporting notes, drafts and edits so AI could learn from them, and turned it down.
score_reason: Pool score kept: first-hand look at a new market for professionals' working papers; one account.
importance_line: Journalists and other professionals may be offered money for their working papers, which could expose sources and hand over rights permanently, but this is one writer’s account and Handshake says the program is not journalism-specific.
summary: In a first-person piece for the Columbia Journalism Review, a freelance journalist describes being offered $1,000 per “case” of at least 50 reporting documents by Handshake, a job-search platform that also runs an AI-training business. The draft contract would have given Handshake a perpetual, irrevocable licence to use the documents, and the writer declined; Handshake’s chief communications officer, Stephen Rocco Rodi, said the program exists because AI models are weak at the work behind finished products.
notes: Contract terms quoted from the article’s description of the draft. Handshake AI revenue and lab figures are the author’s, not independently checked.
